attestations.gloss: The recoverable fragments seem to say something about chicks: that in some case more should remain alive; if all the chicks die, similarly something will die; because it was night the speaker could not give more chicks; even if they had given them, something would have happened; the care is very pleasant/sweet and without pain. This is only a rough impression from isolated Latin words, not a continuous sense.
anomalies: Opening syntax is not Latin: "ETIAM | QUOD | IN | TALI | CUR | PLICARE | U | UEL | AT | PULLO" strings particles and fragments without a governed construction; "PLICARE" is an infinitive hanging without sense.
Non-words or badly corrupted forms: "TREUITER", "RLURES" (probably intended "PLURES"), "ETER", "TITUR", "APPLIS", "PULLUSA", "DATER", "DATUISSEMUS", "TERASSEM", "DEDECTU", "POTESTQUITUS", "EUA".
The clause "UT | RLURES | MANERENT | UIUI" is partly recoverable as "ut plures manerent vivi", but as written "RLURES" is not a Latin word.
"ET | DIE | PRO | CERTO | ETER | LITE | TITUR" contains Latin pieces but no intelligible syntax; "ETER LITE TITUR" is not parseable Latin.
"SI | AUTEM | OMNES | PULLI | MORIETANTUR" uses a malformed verb; classical/medieval Latin would expect something like "morientur" or "morirentur", not "morietantur".
"ET | SIMILITER | MORIETATU" repeats the malformed death-verb and lacks a subject or finite form acceptable as Latin.
"ET | QUIA | SEMEL | APPLIS | UI | L | PULLUSA | QUI | OMNE | MORIETANTUR" has scattered Latin particles but broken morphology and agreement: "PULLUSA", "OMNE" with plural sense, and "MORIETANTUR".
"ET | QUIA | I | NOCTE | ERAT | NON | POTUI | PLURES | PULLOS | DATER" is almost recoverable as "quia in nocte erat, non potui plures pullos dare", but "I" and "DATER" are not acceptable as written.
"ETSI | DATUISSEMUS | L | TERASSEM | EUM | DEI | TR | TIA" has a recognizable concessive "etsi" but the following forms do not make coherent Latin.
"SED | DEDECTU | PULL | RUM | MORIETATURA" is fragmented; "PULL RUM" may conceal "pullorum", but "DEDECTU" and "MORIETATURA" do not yield a normal clause.
"ET | IST | CURA | EST | MULTUM | SUAUI | ET | SINE | DOLORET" is partly Latin-like, perhaps "ista cura est multum suavis et sine dolore", but "IST", case/agreement, and "DOLORET" are wrong.
Final "ET | D | RI | POTESTQUITUS | EUA" is not recoverable Latin.
attestations.uncertainty_note: Some individual corruptions look like OCR/cipher-letter errors concealing plausible Latin phrases, especially around "plures manerent vivi" and "non potui plures pullos dare". I am less sure whether a known manuscript context could explain some isolated abbreviations, but the density of malformed words and failed syntax is too high to accept as a genuine reading.

attestations.gloss: The text seems to be trying to say something about chicks/pullos: that more might remain alive; if all the chicks died, someone or something likewise died; because it was night the speaker could not have more chicks; if they had had them, the speaker would have freed/saved someone, but through lack of chicks he/she/it was dying; it then calls this a cure/care that is very pleasant and painless. Much of the connective and object structure is unrecoverable.
anomalies: "ETIAMQUODINTALICURPLICARE" contains recognizable pieces (etiam quod in tali, perhaps cur, plicare) but no coherent Latin clause as written.
"UTRLURES" looks like a corruption of "ut plures", but "rlures" is not a Latin word.
"MANERENTUIUI" can be read as "manerent vivi", but the fused form and following syntax are damaged.
"ETHIEPROCERTOEAERLIBEBITUR" includes possible "et hic/pro certo" but "eaer libebitur" is not intelligible Latin; "libebitur" is especially suspect here.
"SIAUTEMOMNESPULLIMORIEBANTUREASIMILITERMORIEBATU" has Latin words, but the tense/person/ending and reference are broken: "moriebatu" is not a valid form, and "ea similiter" is syntactically unclear.
"ETQUIASEMELAPPLISUILPULLISAQUIOMNEMORIEBANTUR" has several non-words or corruptions: "APPLISUIL", "AQUI", and a mismatched "omne moriebantur" if that is intended.
"ETQUIAINOCTEERATNONPOTUIPLURESPULLOSHABERET" shifts from first-person "non potui" to third-person/subjunctive "haberet" in a way that does not make a coherent clause.
"SIHABUISSEMUSLBERASSEMEUMDEIARTIA" has possible "si habuissemus" and "liberassem eum", but "LBERASSEM" is misspelled/corrupt and "DEIARTIA" is not intelligible Latin.
"SEDDEFECTUPULLRUMMORIEBATURA" has possible "sed defectu pullorum", but "PULLRUM" and "MORIEBATURA" are corrupt; the latter is not a valid finite verb form.

"ETISTCURAESTMULTUMSUAUIETSINEDOLORE" is close to Latin, perhaps "et ista cura est multum suavis et sine dolore", but as written "ist" is incomplete and "multum suavi" is grammatically off unless heavily emended.
"ETFRIPOTESTQUIBUSEUA" is not recoverable as Latin; "FRI" and "EUA" are not meaningful in this context.
attestations.uncertainty_note: I am least sure whether some of the odd spans are abbreviation scars from a medical or veterinary recipe, since phrases like "defectu pullorum" and "ista cura est ... sine dolore" could belong to a real text. Even allowing for such damage, the corruption is too pervasive for the candidate to stand as a solved reading.

attestations.gloss: Only a very rough topic can be guessed: something about pullets/chicks, keeping more alive, perhaps mating/assigning them, and giving more pullets; it ends with a claim that some care is very pleasant and without pay/salary. Clause-level sense is mostly unrecoverable because the words do not form sustained Latin syntax.
anomalies: "IN | TALI | CUR | PLICARE | U | UEL | AN | PULLA" has no coherent Latin construction; "CUR" as 'why' followed by infinitive "PLICARE" and isolated "U" is syntactically broken.
"TREUITER" is not a Latin word as written; perhaps a corruption of "breviter" or similar, but the span "ET | TREUITER | UT" does not parse.
"RLURES" is a non-word, likely intended for "plures", but as written in "UT | RLURES | MANERENT | UIUI" it is damaged.
"ET | DIE | PRA | CERTA | EXER | LITE | TITUR" is a run of fragments/non-words; "pra", "exer", "titur" are not functioning Latin words here.
"SI | AUTEM | AMNES | PULLI | MARIETANTUR": "amnes" means rivers, not 'all' (probably "omnes"), and "marietantur" is not standard Latin; the clause is semantically and morphologically suspect.
"EX | SIMILITER | MARIETATU" is ungrammatical; "ex" has no object and "marietatu" is not a normal form.
"SEMEL | APPLIS | UI | L | PULLISI" contains multiple non-words or isolated letters and cannot be construed.
"QUI | AMNE | MARIETANTUR" has apparent corruption of "omne/omnes" and the same nonstandard "marietantur"; agreement and sense are broken.
"I | NACTE | ERAT | NAN | PATUI" includes isolated "I", non-word/odd form "nacte", and "nan" for perhaps "non"; the syntax is not Latin as written.
"PLURES | PULLAS | DATER" has a non-Latin verb form "dater" in this context; perhaps "dare", but the clause is broken.
"ETSI | DATUISSEMUS | L | TERASSEM | EUM" includes the non-form "datuissemus" and isolated "L"; "terassem" is not normal Latin.
"SEI | XR | TIA | SES | SERECTU | PULL | RUM | MARIETATURI" is largely fragmentary/non-Latin, with isolated letters and split words; no recoverable syntax.
"SINE | SALAREN" seems to aim at "sine salario" but "salaren" is not a Latin form.
"ET | R | RI | PATESTQUITUS | EUA" is not Latin; isolated letters plus "patestquitus" and "eua" yield no parse.
attestations.uncertainty_note: Some repeated forms may reflect a medieval or documentary technical vocabulary about poultry, and several corruptions are close to Latin words such as "plures", "omnes", "dare", or "salario". Still, the density of non-words and broken syntax makes the exact reading impossible to accept as genuine Latin text.

attestations.gloss: The recoverable sense seems to concern chicks: somehow arranging or explaining matters so that more might remain alive; if all the chicks were dying/died similarly; because once something was applied to the chicks, all were dying; because it was night the writer could not give more chicks, even if they had given them; by God's/Christ's grace perhaps, but because of a lack/defect of chicks they would die; and this care/cure is very pleasant and without pain, with a final clause largely unrecoverable.
anomalies: "CUR PLICARE U UEL AB PULLO" does not form a clear Latin phrase; "plicare" is possible, but the construction is broken.
"NREUITER" is not a Latin word as written, though it may intend "breviter".
"RLURES" is not a Latin word as written, likely "plures".
"DIE PRO CERTO EXER LINE NITUR" is syntactically and lexically incoherent; "exer line nitur" is not readable Latin.
"MORIENANTUR" / "MORIENATU" recur as nonstandard forms; they seem to intend something like "moriebantur" or "morientur" but are not acceptable as written.
"EX SIMALITER" is ungrammatical; "simaliter" is not classical/medieval Latin as written for "similiter".
"SEMEL APPLIS UI L PULLISA" is a run of broken forms; only "semel" is clear.
"QUI OMNE MORIENANTUR" has agreement/syntax problems: "qui" with "omne" and the corrupt verb form do not cohere.
"PULLOS DANER" and "DANUISSEMUS" are non-forms; they may point to "dare" / "dedissemus" or similar but are not Latin as written.
"L NERASSEM EUM DEI XR TIA" is highly damaged; "DEI XR TIA" may conceal "Dei/Christi gratia," but the clause is unreadable.
"DEAECTU PULL RUM MORIENATURA" appears to intend "defectu pullorum ..." but is broken and syntactically incomplete.
"SINE DOLOREB" has an impossible ending; expected "dolore" or similar.
"A RI POTESTQUINUS EUA" is not recoverable Latin; "potest" is visible, but the surrounding string is nonsensical.
attestations.uncertainty_note: I am least sure whether the many malformed words reflect a heavily damaged but systematic transcription of a genuine Latin original, since several errors look like plausible letter confusions. Even allowing for that, the text as presented is too pervasively corrupt to read as an acceptable solved decipherment.

attestations.gloss: The recoverable fragments seem to say something about chicks/young birds: that in some circumstance more would remain alive; if all the chicks died, similarly something else would die; because it was night the writer could not have/obtain more chicks; there is mention of care being very pleasant and without pain. Much of the wording between these fragments is not interpretable as Latin clauses.
anomalies: "CUR PLICARE U UEL AS PULLO" does not form a Latin phrase; "U" and "AS" are unexplained fragments and the syntax around "plicare" is broken.
"TREUITER" is not a recognizable Latin word in this context.
"RLURES" looks like a damaged/non-word form, perhaps intended for "plures".
"PRO CERTO ETER LITE TITUR" contains real-looking pieces but no coherent Latin construction; "ETER" and "TITUR" are fragmentary/non-words as written.
"OMNES PULLI MORIETANTUR" is intelligible in intent, but "morietantur" is not a normal Latin form for 'will die' or 'may die'.
"SIMLLITER MORIETATU" has misspelling/non-form: "simlliter" for perhaps "similiter", and "morietatu" is not a valid finite form.
"APPLIS UI L PULLASI QUI OMNE MORIETANTUR" is heavily broken: "applis", isolated "UI L", "pullasi", and singular "omne" with plural sense do not make a Latin clause.
"ET QUIA L NOCTE ERAT" has an unexplained isolated "L" and awkward syntax.
"NON POTUI PLURES PULLOS PATER" is not grammatical as written; "pater" is 'father' or a verb form in other contexts, not fitting after "potui plures pullos".
"ETSI PATUISSEMUS L TERASSEM EUM" is syntactically incoherent, with isolated "L" and unclear "terassem".
"DEI TR TIA" consists of fragments rather than a Latin phrase.
"DEDECTU PULL RUM MORIETATURI" is broken: "dedectu" is suspect, "pull rum" is split, and "morietaturi" is a participial/future-looking form without clear agreement or construction.
"IST CURA EST MULTUM SUAUI" has nonstandard "ist" and case/adverb problems around "multum suaui".
"SINE DOLORES" is wrong case for a normal Latin phrase; one expects "sine doloribus" or similar.
"D RI POTESTQUITUS EUA" is not recoverable Latin; "potestquitus" and "eua" do not form a valid ending.
attestations.uncertainty_note: Some spans could be abbreviation scars or OCR-like misreadings of a real Latin original, especially where near-words appear ("RLURES" for "PLURES", "SIMLLITER" for "SIMILITER"). But the density of malformed words and broken syntax is too high to accept the candidate as genuine Latin as it stands.
